{{nihongo|'''Muraya-ni-masu-Mifutsuhime Shrine'''|村屋坐弥冨都比売神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

It is a {{ill|Shikinai Taisha|ja|式内大社|simple|Shikinai Taisha|qid=Q134917288}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|ja|社格|ko|사격 (신토)|zh|社格|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural shrine}}. The shrine stands facing the “Nakatsu-michi” (Tachibana Highway), one of the {{ill|Three Yamato Roads|Q11433382|qid=Q11433382|lt=Three Yamato Roads}}.

The principal enshrined deity is {{ill|Mihotsuhime-no-Mikoto|ja|三穂津姫|zh|三穗津姬|qid=Q6378698|lt=Miho-tsu-hime no Mikoto}} (also known as Mifutsuhime-gami), with {{ill|Ōmononushi|fr|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主|mni|ꯑꯣꯃꯣꯅꯣꯅꯨꯁꯤ|ru|Омононуси|simple|Ōmononushi|zh|大物主|qid=Q10936701|lt=Ōmononushi no Mikoto}} enshrined as an accompanying deity. Miho-tsu-hime no Mikoto is the consort deity of {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi no Mikoto}}, and in the myths recorded in the *Kojiki* and *Nihon Shoki*, Ōmononushi and Ōkuninushi are regarded as the same deity. Ōmononushi no Mikoto is the enshrined deity of {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|Q705542|qid=Q705542}}, and this shrine, which enshrines his consort deity, is considered a branch shrine of Ōmiwa Shrine.

===History===
=== Overview ===
The date of the shrine’s founding is unknown. According to the *{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}*, during the {{ill|Jinshin War|Q2378252|qid=Q2378252}} in the first year of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ar|الإمبراطور تيمو|arz|الامبراطور تيمو|azb|تمو|ca|Tenmu|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر تێنمو|cs|Temmu|de|Temmu|eo|Temmu|es|Tenmu Tennō|fa|امپراتور تنمو|fr|Tenmu|hak|Tenmu Thiên-fòng|he|טמו, קיסר יפן|hu|Tenmu japán császár|id|Kaisar Tenmu|it|Tenmu|ja|天武天皇|ka|ტენმუ|ko|덴무 천황|nl|Tenmu|pl|Tenmu|pt|Tenmu|ru|Император Тэмму|sh|Car Temmu|simple|Emperor Tenmu|sl|Cesar Tenmu|su|Kaisar Temmu|sv|Tenmu|th|จักรพรรดิเท็มมุ|tl|Emperador Temmu|tr|Temmu (imparator)|uk|Імператор Темму|vi|Thiên hoàng Tenmu|yo|Emperor Temmu|zh|天武天皇|zh_min_nan|Tenmu Thian-hông|zh_yue|天武天皇|qid=Q335181}}’s reign ({{ill|673|Q31105|qid=Q31105}}), the Muraya deity delivered a {{ill|Oracle|Q217123|qid=Q217123}} to {{ill|Ōtomo no Fukei|Q11432333|qid=Q11432333}}, who was on the side of Prince Ōama, saying, “The enemy is coming, so block the Nakatsu-michi.” In recognition of this service, a {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} was conferred upon the deity. This is the earliest recorded instance of the bestowal of a divine rank. Records such as the Yamato Province Tax Register ({{ill|Shōsōin Documents|Q11545362|qid=Q11545362}}) and the {{ill|Shinshō Kyakuchokufushō|Q11502312|qid=Q11502312}} note that the imperial court made repeated donations of {{ill|Shinpo|Q1689534|qid=Q1689534}} to the shrine. In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, the shrine is listed as a major shrine and is recorded as receiving offerings at the Tsukinami, Aename, and Niiname festivals.

In Shōwa 2 ({{ill|1926|Q5259|qid=Q5259}}), the shrine was elevated to the rank of prefectural shrine.

{{quotation|
'''“Emperor Tenmu, Upper Volume,” *Nihon Shoki, Lower Volume*, Kodansha Academic Library'''<br/>
“Then the deity Muraya (Moriya Shrine) possessed the priest (shinkan) and said, ‘An army will come along the road within my shrine grounds. Therefore, block the shrine road.’”
}}

=== Subsidiary Shrines ===
;Sessha Muraya Shrine (むらやじんじゃ)
: A Shikinaisha. Enshrined deities: {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|Q2564508|qid=Q2564508|lt=Ame-no-Koyane no Mikoto}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|lt=Futsunushi|Q1107286|qid=Q1107286|qid=Q1107286|lt=Futsunushi no Kami}}, {{ill|Himegami|Q22070227|qid=Q22070227|lt=Hime no Ōkami}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|lt=Takemikazuchi|Q1502690|qid=Q1502690|qid=Q1502690|lt=Takemikazuchi no Kami}}, as well as Ōtomo no Takemochi no Muraji and Muroya no Muraji.
: Formerly located on the riverside east of the current site at the place name Miyanoyama, but it was destroyed by warfare in {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 12 and subsequently relocated to the present shrine grounds.
;Massha Hattori Shrine (はっとりじんじゃ)
: A Shikinaisha. Enshrined deities: {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|Q2842779|qid=Q2842779|lt=Ame-no-Minakanushi no Mikoto}}, {{ill|amenomihokonomikoto|Q119380365|qid=Q119380365|lt=Ame-no-Mihoko no Mikoto}}.
: Formerly located at Kakimori in Ōaza Daianji, it was destroyed by warfare during the Nanboku-chō period and relocated to the present shrine grounds in Tenshō 1 ({{ill|1573|Q6678|qid=Q6678}}).
;Sessha Kusumi Shrine (Wakamiya Ebisu Shrine) (くすすみじんじゃ)
: A Shikinaisha. Enshrined deities: Ame-no-Kunohi no Mikoto and {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi no Mikoto}}.
: Formerly located on the riverside east of the current site at Ebisu-yama, it was relocated to the present shrine grounds in Keiō 2.
;Massha Ichikishimahime Shrine (いちきしまひめじんじゃ) and Mononobe Shrine (もののべじんじゃ)
: Enshrined deities: Kashiwaya-hime no Mikoto and Umashimaji no Mikoto; accompanying enshrinement of Mononobe no Moriya no Muraji. Their origins are unknown, but they are said to enshrine the ancestral deities of the shrine families, particularly the Moriya family.

=== Access ===
* About a 30-minute walk west from {{ill|Makimuku Station|Q4980794|qid=Q4980794}} on the {{ill|Sakurai Line|Q865801|qid=Q865801}} of {{ill|West Japan Railway Company|Q502125|qid=Q502125|lt=JR West}}
* About a 40-minute walk east from {{ill|Tawaramoto Station|Q7689224|qid=Q7689224}} on the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kashihara Line}} of {{ill|Kintetsu Railway|Q1531085|qid=Q1531085|lt=Kintetsu Railway}}
